correctness.rationale: The argument integrates the two triangular sectors of [0,pi]^2 exactly. Twice integrating by parts gives the signed antipodal boundary contribution (-1)^n f'(pi)/(pi n^2) plus an o(n^-2) cosine transform by Riemann--Lebesgue, certifying infinitely many negative coefficients for f'(pi) nonzero. The exponential is integrated exactly for constant, axial and mixed frequencies, with strict sign checks including equality n^2=Q(a). Compact abelian Bochner gives equivalence to the finite-matrix criterion. Standalone code independently checks 24 integral comparisons (error below 1.3e-7), 1,497 axial signs, 432 mixed signs, and negative finite matrices; these numerical diagnostics are not used as the general proof.

value.rationale: The product supremum metric is natural in simultaneous phase measurements and tensor product circle geometry. The exponential profile is automatically a valid kernel on the corresponding unwrapped Euclidean l-infinity plane (factorization into one-dimensional Laplace kernels) and on each separate circle, so the loss of positivity after wrapping both factors is a nontrivial structural boundary. The all-C^2 antipodal derivative obstruction diagnoses the mechanism beyond a special example; the exact all-frequency Q(a) boundary and exponentially growing first bad frequency quantify how finite resolution can conceal invalid covariances.
